caption: The drawing consists of several woven patterns and diagrams, primarily in dark blue and white. In the upper left corner, there is a small diagram labeled “Tabby,” “Overshot thread,” “Wool,” and “Linen,” showing the structure and layering of weaving threads in blue and outlined in black. Adjacent to this, toward the upper right, there is a rectangular section depicting an overall geometric floral pattern, bordered by a thin frame, also in blue and white. The main and largest section in the center and lower half of the image is a detailed rectangular textile design with floral motifs in white on a dark blue background, including roses and starburst shapes, along with stylized leaves. The left side of the main segment features a vertical strip with a diamond lattice border and white animal figures resembling birds. Below this segment, a rectangular label space reads "MARY HEBARD ORANGE 1841" in white text on a blue background. Beneath the main floral design is a horizontal band with stylized symmetrical white shapes, resembling arches and tulips, on a blue ground. The entire composition is enclosed by a narrow diamond-patterned border in blue and white. The drawing is marked “HOWARD H. SHERMAN '36” in the lower right corner.
title: Handwoven Coverlet
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
